subject: Re: Luminex pilot — call-shape declaration & GPU-fit questions
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@luminex.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Luminex pilot — initial call-shape dump and a couple questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to scope the pilot. Per our conversation, I attached a small sample of our production telemetry plus a high-level CSV that summarizes session-level stats. Quick context: we operate a hybrid product with both interactive chat (support assistant) and batched analysis requests (document summarization).

Couple of specifics we flagged for sizing:
- Avg concurrent interactive sessions: ~210 during business hours, with a p95 burst to ~760 for ~7 minutes daily.
- Typical interactive prompt length: 40–120 tokens, responses 60–900 tokens (long tails from doc retrieval).
- Batch jobs: 12 parallel workers that submit multi-turn prompts; each worker averages 18 requests per hour during nightly windows.
- We use a lot of context reuse (KV cache hits ~38%), which we hope helps keep cost down.

Can you confirm how Redwood would treat the mixed workload for Dedicated capacity planning? We want to ensure reserved GPU pools and burst capacity map correctly to both session types. Also: what telemetry would you need to make an accurate GPU-fit recommendation?

Attaching: luminex_callshape_sample.csv and a quick histogram.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
Luminex AI

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@luminex.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Luminex pilot — call-shape dump and a couple questions

Alex — thanks for the dump, this is perfect to start. A few quick clarifying Qs before we run a sizing sketch: 

1) When you say "p95 burst to ~760 for ~7 minutes daily" — is that a sustained steady burst (flat at 760) or a stepped fan-in (peaks above then dips)? Also is that burst concentrated to a single region?

2) For the batch workers: are the 12 workers independent processes (each with their own session/LLM state) or are they submitting stateless requests into a queue? If independent, do they long-poll and keep KV cache warm between requests?

3) Can you share a small sample of latency SLO targets for these two classes (interactive vs batch) — e.g., interactive p95 target and acceptable p99 tail?

Operational notes on our side (so you know what the recommendation will consider):
- We size Dedicated pools by accounting for steady-state concurrency + a configurable burst cushion.
- Interactive workloads are prioritized for low p95 latency and benefit greatly from session-level KV cache retention.
- Batch workers are often cost-optimized to run on quantized variants and can tolerate higher tail latency.

If you can confirm those 3 bullets and drop a 24-hour minute-level concurrency trace (even a 1440-row CSV) we can produce a first-pass GPU-fit. If easier, fill the "callshape-survey.xlsx" (I attached a blank template) and we’ll run the calculator.

I’ll loop Marissa for the proposal worksheet if we get the traces.

Cheers,
Mateo
Pre-Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@luminex.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Luminex pilot — call-shape dump and a couple questions

Hi Mateo — answers below and attaching a 24h minute-level trace (luminex_callshape_sample.csv) plus prompt/response length histograms:

1) Burst shape: it's a stepped fan-in. We hit short spikes up to ~940 for ~30-90s then settle around 700 for a 5–10 minute plateau. It’s single-region (us-west).

2) Batch workers: they are independent long-running processes that keep local state and try to re-use context where possible. Each worker submits multi-turn sequences, so yes KV cache is warm in many cases.

3) SLO targets: interactive p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 450ms. Batch jobs are ok at p95 <= 2.5s.

Notes: we are open to quantized model variants for batch; interactive must use FP16 model variant. Also attaching the callshape-survey.xlsx filled out for the pilot parameters.

Thanks — let me know if you want any more telemetry fields.

—Alex

Attachments: luminex_callshape_sample.csv (1440 rows), prompt_and_response_histogram.png, callshape-survey.xlsx

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@luminex.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Luminex pilot — call-shape dump and a couple questions

Alex — great, this is very actionable. Summary & next steps: 

Summary of key inputs we’ll use for a GPU-fit sketch:
- Region: us-west; steady-state interactive concurrency ~210, typical p95 bursts ~700 with short spikes to ~940 (30–90s).
- Prompt/response: interactive median prompt ~75 tokens, median response ~220 tokens; long-tail responses up to ~900 tokens. KV cache reuse ~38%.
- Batch: 12 independent workers, multi-turn, KV cache warm, tolerant p95 up to 2.5s; ok to use quantized models for cost efficiency.
- SLOs: interactive p95 180ms / p99 450ms; batch p95 2.5s.

Preliminary sizing assumptions we will apply (we’ll produce a spreadsheets-backed recommendation):
- Reserve a dedicated pool sized to handle steady-state concurrency + a 20% cushion for short bursts.
- Configure a separate burst pool (on-demand/dedicated-burst) that can absorb the 700->940 short spikes; we’ll model autoscale warm-up and cold-start assumptions.
- Prioritize FP16 model variants on interactive pool; use q4/bit8 quantized variants for batch where possible.
- Account for KV cache warm reuse: effective token cost reduced by ~30–40% on interactive flows.

Action items:
1) Marissa — can you run the quick calculator and draft a two-option proposal (Conservative reserve vs Optimized reserve) and include estimated monthly committed cost + expected on-demand burst spend? Please reference deal LXN-2027-PLT-003.
2) Karthik — can you validate the GPU SKUs for the us-west region and add runbook notes for session affinity / KV cache retention TTLs we should recommend?
3) Alex — if possible, share a small sample of model sizes used for interactive vs batch (base model name + typical batch size / seq length) — that will tighten the recommendation.

We’ll aim to deliver the first-pass GPU-fit and a one-page tradeoff memo by EOD Thu (two business days). If that timeline is tight, tell us and we’ll adjust.

Thanks — excited to get this going.

Best,
Mateo
Pre-Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
